commit dd745ae6a4d6bad068c77b87dccb2b4b1c88c308
Author: Da-Wei Lee &lt;daviddwlee84@gmail.com&gt;
Date:   Wed May 27 14:36:21 2026 +0800

    feat(visidata): ship dot_visidatarc + vd-arrow alias to dodge pandas StringDtype feather crash
    
    VisiData 3.3's bundled .feather loader (loaders/_pandas.py → PandasSheet →
    pd.read_feather → dtype_to_type → np.issubdtype) crashes on any column the
    file's schema metadata marks as numpy_type=string — i.e. any DataFrame
    written from pandas ≥ 2.0 with string columns. Error reads e.g.
    &#96;ValueError: Could not convert ... dtype: string to a NumPy dtype
    (via .dtype value &lt;StringDtype(na_value=&lt;NA&gt;)&gt;)&#96;. The dtype identity
    travels inside the feather metadata, so downgrading pandas / pyarrow in
    the visidata tool venv does NOT help (verified pandas 2.3.x + pyarrow
    16/18/24 all repro).
    
    Fix:
    - dot_visidatarc: setattr(VisiData, 'open_feather', …) reroute to the
      bundled pure-pyarrow ArrowSheet loader (loaders/arrow.py), which never
      touches pandas. End-to-end verified: &#96;visidata -b sz_*.feather -o csv&#96;
      now writes 443 rows instead of 0 + ValueError.
    - dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh: add &#96;vd-arrow='visidata -f arrow'&#96;
      escape hatch for hosts where the rc file isn't deployed yet or for
      explicit/debug invocation.
    - pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md: symptom-first
      diagnosis (verbatim error grep-able), version matrix, upstream loader
      refs, trade-offs of the override.
    - dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml: replace stale
      comment on the &#96;pyarrow&#96; dep (the previous "to be able open feather
      file" was misleading once we learned pyarrow alone doesn't fix it).
    
    Co-authored-by: Cursor &lt;cursoragent@cursor.com&gt;

 .../roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml        |   7 +-
 dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh                     |  10 +
 dot_visidatarc                                     |  64 ++++++
 pitfalls/README.md                                 |   1 +
 .../visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md    | 215 +++++++++++++++++++++
 5 files changed, 296 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

Author: Da-Wei Lee &lt;daviddwlee84@gmail.com&gt;
Date:   Wed May 27 14:36:21 2026 +0800

    feat(visidata): ship dot_visidatarc + vd-arrow alias to dodge pandas StringDtype feather crash
    
    VisiData 3.3's bundled .feather loader (loaders/_pandas.py → PandasSheet →
    pd.read_feather → dtype_to_type → np.issubdtype) crashes on any column the
    file's schema metadata marks as numpy_type=string — i.e. any DataFrame
    written from pandas ≥ 2.0 with string columns. Error reads e.g.
    &#96;ValueError: Could not convert ... dtype: string to a NumPy dtype
    (via .dtype value &lt;StringDtype(na_value=&lt;NA&gt;)&gt;)&#96;. The dtype identity
    travels inside the feather metadata, so downgrading pandas / pyarrow in
    the visidata tool venv does NOT help (verified pandas 2.3.x + pyarrow
    16/18/24 all repro).
    
    Fix:
    - dot_visidatarc: setattr(VisiData, 'open_feather', …) reroute to the
      bundled pure-pyarrow ArrowSheet loader (loaders/arrow.py), which never
      touches pandas. End-to-end verified: &#96;visidata -b sz_*.feather -o csv&#96;
      now writes 443 rows instead of 0 + ValueError.
    - dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh: add &#96;vd-arrow='visidata -f arrow'&#96;
      escape hatch for hosts where the rc file isn't deployed yet or for
      explicit/debug invocation.
    - pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md: symptom-first
      diagnosis (verbatim error grep-able), version matrix, upstream loader
      refs, trade-offs of the override.
    - dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml: replace stale
      comment on the &#96;pyarrow&#96; dep (the previous "to be able open feather
      file" was misleading once we learned pyarrow alone doesn't fix it).
    
    Co-authored-by: Cursor &lt;cursoragent@cursor.com&gt;

diff --git a/pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md b/pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d65792b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/pitfalls/visidata-feather-stringdtype-numpy-dtype.md
@@ -0,0 +1,215 @@
+# VisiData 3.3 crashes opening &#96;.feather&#96; saved with pandas StringDtype — &#96;Could not convert ... to a NumPy dtype&#96; / &#96;Cannot interpret '&lt;StringDtype(na_value=&lt;NA&gt;)&gt;' as a data type&#96;
+
+**Symptoms** (grep this section):
+
+- &#96;visidata foo.feather&#96; opens, prints &#96;opening foo.feather as feather&#96;, then dies with
+  &#96;&#96;&#96;text
+  ValueError: Could not convert 0  sz-123251-d5442447
+  1  sz-123258-d54458be
+  ...
+  Name: client_order_id, Length: 443, dtype: string to a NumPy dtype
+  (via &#96;.dtype&#96; value &lt;StringDtype(na_value=&lt;NA&gt;)&gt;).
+  &#96;&#96;&#96;
+- Or, with older pandas (2.x): same &#96;ValueError&#96; but trailing string is
+  &#96;string[python]&#96; instead of &#96;&lt;StringDtype(na_value=&lt;NA&gt;)&gt;&#96;.
+- VisiData status pane shows &#96;raw() returned ERR&#96;; sheet has 0 rows / 1 dummy col.
+- Pure &#96;pd.read_feather('foo.feather')&#96; succeeds — file is well-formed.
+- Other &#96;.feather&#96; files from the same producer (or earlier days) open fine —
+  only files whose **schema metadata** has &#96;numpy_type: string&#96; trigger it.
+
+**First seen**: 2026-05
+**Affects**: VisiData ≥ 2.0 (the broken code path has existed since pandas 2.0
+shipped &#96;StringDtype&#96;) — surfaces whenever the **feather file's embedded
+pandas metadata** marks any column as &#96;StringDtype&#96;, which any DataFrame
+written from pandas ≥ 2.0 + pyarrow ≥ 7 will do by default for &#96;string&#96; cols.
+v3.3 (latest on PyPI as of 2026-05) is unfixed; no relevant issue/PR upstream.
+**Status**: workaround documented (this repo ships
+[&#96;dot_visidatarc&#96;](../dot_visidatarc) — auto-routes &#96;.feather&#96; to the pure-arrow
+loader; explicit per-invocation escape hatch via the &#96;vd-arrow&#96; alias in
+[&#96;dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh&#96;](../dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh)).
+
+## Symptom
+
+&#96;&#96;&#96;text
+$ visidata sz_2026-05-13.feather
+saul.pw/VisiData v3.3
+opening sz_2026-05-13.feather as feather
+ValueError: Could not convert 0      sz-123251-d5442447
+1      sz-123258-d54458be
+...
+442    sz-128142-1e672faf
+Name: client_order_id, Length: 443, dtype: string to a NumPy dtype

VisiData already has many vim-style bindings built in like `gg`/`G` for navigation and `/` for search, so the real opportunity for a vim mode would be remapping keys like `i` to enter edit mode instead of `e`, which aligns with vim conventions. I should check what other rebindings would make sense for vim users and look into the VisiData version to understand the XDG config support mentioned, then search the repo for any existing VisiData configurations.</details></think>

vd(1)                        Quick Reference Guide                       vd(1)

NAME
     VisiData — a terminal utility for exploring and arranging tabular data

SYNOPSIS
     vd [options] [input ...]
     visidata [options] [input ...]
     vd [options] --play cmdlog [-w waitsecs] [--batch] [-i] [-o output]
        [field=value]
     vd [options] [input ...] +toplevel:subsheet:row:col

DESCRIPTION
     VisiData is an easy-to-use multipurpose tool to explore, clean, edit, and
     restructure data. Rows can be selected, filtered, and grouped; columns
     can be rearranged, transformed, and derived via regex or Python expres‐
     sions; and workflows can be saved, documented, and replayed.

   REPLAY MODE
     -p, --play=cmdlog       replay a saved cmdlog within the interface
     -w, --replay-wait=seconds
                             wait seconds between commands
     -b, --batch             replay in batch mode (with no interface)
     -i, --interactive       launch VisiData in interactive mode after batch
     -o, --output=file       save final visible sheet to file as .tsv
     field=value             replace "{field}" in cmdlog contents with value

   Commands During Replay
        ^K                   cancel current replay

   GLOBAL COMMANDS
     All keystrokes are case sensitive. The ^ prefix is shorthand for Ctrl.

   Keystrokes to start off with
      ^Q              abort program immediately
      ^C              cancel user input or abort all async threads on current
                      sheet
     g^C              abort all secondary threads
       q              quit current sheet or menu
       Q              quit current sheet and free associated memory
      gq              quit all sheets (clean exit)

     Alt+H            activate help menu (Enter/left-mouse to expand submenu
                      or execute command)
     g^H              view this man page
     z^H              view sheet of command longnames and keybindings for cur‐
                      rent sheet

      gb              open sidebar in a new sheet
       b              toggle sidebar

```
有，**如果你依賴 VisiData / appdirs 的預設路徑，macOS 跟 Linux 會不一樣**。

關鍵點是：VisiData 的 XDG 支援其實分成兩層：

1. **主設定檔**

   * 舊路徑仍是 `~/.visidatarc`
   * 也支援 `config.py`，目前文件說如果 `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/visidata/config.py` 存在，會被當作 default config 載入。
   * 當初 PR #1420 做法是用 `appdirs.user_config_dir("visidata") / "config.py"` 優先於 `~/.visidatarc`。

2. **`visidata_dir`**

   * 這是放 plugins、macros、input history 這類 VisiData 額外檔案的目錄。
   * VisiData 3.2 才把 default `visidata_dir` 改成 XDG / appdirs 位置。
   * 但這個改動主要是針對原本的 `~/.visidata` 目錄，不是把 `~/.visidatarc` 全面改掉；維護者在 PR 裡也明確回覆過「只針對 `.visidata` repo/dir」。

真正麻煩點在 **appdirs 對 macOS 的判斷不是 `~/.config`**：

```text
Linux / Unix:
  user_config_dir("visidata") -> ~/.config/visidata
  或 $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/visidata

macOS:
  user_config_dir("visidata") -> ~/Library/Preferences/visidata
```

appdirs 原始碼文件/邏輯就是這樣：Mac config 走 `~/Library/Preferences/`，Unix 才走 `~/.config` 或 `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`。

所以你截圖裡的問題，**我會選 A：用 `VD_CONFIG` + `VD_DIR` 明確指定到 `~/.config/visidata`**。這比 symlink 乾淨，且是 VisiData 自己支援的 override；目前程式碼會讀 `VD_DIR` / `VD_CONFIG` 來覆蓋預設值。

建議放在你的 `dot_config/shell/00_exports.sh.tmpl`：

```sh
# VisiData: keep config path consistent across Linux/macOS.
export VD_DIR="${VD_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/visidata}"
export VD_CONFIG="${VD_CONFIG:-$VD_DIR/config.py}"
```

然後 chezmoi 管理：

```text
dot_config/visidata/config.py.tmpl
```

也就是目標會變成：

```text
~/.config/visidata/config.py
```

這樣 Linux / macOS 都吃同一份 config，不需要在 macOS 建：

```text
~/Library/Preferences/visidata/config.py
```

唯一要注意：`VD_DIR` 不只是 config 目錄，還可能存 macros、plugins、input history。如果你不想讓 mutable state 混進 `~/.config/visidata`，可以只固定 `VD_CONFIG`，而把 `VD_DIR` 放到 data/state 位置；但若你的目標是「兩個 OS 都用同一套 VisiData 目錄」，上面的 A 方案是最直接的。
```

    # VisiData's defaults are already vim-flavored (h/j/k/l nav, gg/G top/bottom,
    # /? search, n/N next/prev, q/Q quit).  The customize-docs canonical
    # add-on for vim users is rebinding &#96;i&#96; from &#96;addcol-incr&#96;
    # (features/incr.py:27) to &#96;edit-cell&#96;, matching vim's INSERT-mode mnemonic.
    # &#96;addcol-incr&#96; remains reachable via the Alt+H command menu or
    # &#96;Space addcol-incr&lt;Enter&gt;&#96;.  Also &#96;e&#96; (the historical edit-cell binding)
    # continues to work — this gate is purely additive on the keystroke &#96;i&#96;.
    # Per https://www.visidata.org/docs/customize/#example-bind-i-to-edit-cell-globally
    from visidata import TableSheet  # noqa: E402
    TableSheet.unbindkey('i')
    TableSheet.bindkey('i', 'edit-cell')
except ImportError:
    # pyarrow / visidata.loaders.arrow not available — leave the default
    # PandasSheet path in place. The user will get the standard pandas
    # error if they hit a StringDtype feather, which is no worse than not
    # having this override at all.
    pass

```

---

Now the follow-up question — **`$` / `_` / `0` / `^` and "go to last column"**:

**Short answer**: VisiData has the operation but bound to `gh` / `gl` (consistent with the `gg`/`G` row-nav pattern), not the strict-vim `$` / `0`. The exact mapping:

| keystroke | currently bound to | vim-purist would want |
|---|---|---|
| `gh` | `go-leftmost` (default — already vim-style) | — |
| `gl` | `go-rightmost` (default — already vim-style) | — |
| `0` | unbound | `go-leftmost` (free slot, no trade-off) |
| `$` | `type-currency` (set col type to $) | `go-rightmost` (trade-off) |
| `_` | `resize-col-max` (auto-fit col width) | `go-leftmost` (trade-off) |
| `^` | `rename-col` (rename column) | `go-leftmost` (trade-off) |

So three valid scopes if you want to add this under `enableVimMode`:

**(A) Conservative — only `0`** (the free slot)
```python
TableSheet.bindkey('0', 'go-leftmost')
```
Zero trade-off. Vim's `^` / `_` / `$` keep their VisiData meanings.

**(B) Standard-vim — `0` + `$`**
```python
TableSheet.bindkey('0', 'go-leftmost')
TableSheet.unbindkey('$')
TableSheet.bindkey('$', 'go-rightmost')
```
Loses single-letter `type-currency` (still reachable via `Space type-currency` or the `Edit > Type` menu). Pure vim-line-nav feel for column navigation.

**(C) Full vim — `0` + `$` + `_` + `^`**
```python
TableSheet.bindkey('0', 'go-leftmost')
TableSheet.unbindkey('$'); TableSheet.bindkey('$', 'go-rightmost')
TableSheet.unbindkey('_'); TableSheet.bindkey('_', 'go-leftmost')
TableSheet.unbindkey('^'); TableSheet.bindkey('^', 'go-leftmost')
```
Adds `resize-col-max` and `rename-col` to the "lost single-letter" list. Both very useful in everyday VisiData. Strong vim parity, but heaviest trade-off.

My recommendation: **(A)** — bind `0` (zero cost) and leave `gh`/`gl` as the primary "vim-style" column endpoints. The `$` / `_` / `^` overrides cost you three frequently-useful single-letter commands (`type-currency`, `resize-col-max`, `rename-col`) — and `gh`/`gl` already give the muscle-memory hit.

Want me to land any of these as a follow-up commit, or leave column nav at VisiData defaults?

import visidata
from visidata import vd, TableSheet, Sheet, BaseSheet

# Use the actual getCommand API (the source of truth for runtime dispatch).
# Need a sheet instance for proper resolution.
sheet = TableSheet('test')

def resolve(key):
    try:
        cmd = sheet.getCommand(key)
        return cmd.longname if cmd else None
    except Exception as e:
        return f'err: {e}'

for key in ['N', 'n', 'y', 'Y', 'z$', 'zw', 'zN', 'gw', '0', '$', '_', '^']:
    print(f'  `{key}` -> {resolve(key)!r}')
EOF

```
@visidata.VisiData.api
def prettykeys(vd, key):
    if not key or '+' in key[:-1]:
        return key

    for k, v in vd.prettykeys_trdict.items():
        key = key.replace(k, v)

    # replace ^ with Ctrl but not if ^ is last char
    key = key[:-1].replace('^', 'Ctrl+')+key[-1]
    # 1497: allow Shift+ for Alt keys
    if key[-1] in string.ascii_uppercase and ('+' not in key or 'Alt+' in key) and '_' not in key:
        key = key[:-1] + 'Shift+' + key[-1]

    return key.strip()

---

  prettykeys('zn') -&gt; 'zn'
  prettykeys('z$') -&gt; 'z$'
  prettykeys('zw') -&gt; 'zw'
  prettykeys('gN') -&gt; 'gShift+N'
  prettykeys('N') -&gt; 'Shift+N'
  prettykeys('iN') -&gt; 'iShift+N'
  prettykeys('gzN') -&gt; 'gzShift+N'

    # --- INSERT mnemonic ----------------------------------------------------

    TableSheet.unbindkey('i')

    # --- Column navigation (vim line-internal chars) ------------------------
    # &#96;0&#96; was unbound by default — free slot, zero trade-off.
    # &#96;$&#96; / &#96;_&#96; / &#96;^&#96; displace useful single-letter commands; we relocate
    # them to mnemonic 2-char slots in the same block so they're not lost.
    #
    #   key  | new action       | displaced from   | relocated to
    #   -----+------------------+------------------+--------------
    #    0   | go-leftmost      | (was unbound)    | -

    #    _   | go-leftmost      | resize-col-max   | zw  (z + Width)

    #

    # and provide a non-overloaded fallback.
    TableSheet.bindkey('0', 'go-leftmost')
    TableSheet.unbindkey('$'); TableSheet.bindkey('$', 'go-rightmost')
    TableSheet.unbindkey('_'); TableSheet.bindkey('_', 'go-leftmost')

    TableSheet.bindkey('z$', 'type-currency')
    TableSheet.bindkey('zw', 'resize-col-max')
    TableSheet.bindkey('zN', 'rename-col')

All five TODOs done. Here's what landed:

## Full-vim VisiData (`enableVimMode=true`) — column navigation summary

Bindings now installed on every `TableSheet`:

| keystroke | new action | displaced from | relocated to |
|---|---|---|---|
| `i` | `edit-cell` (existing — INSERT mnemonic) | `addcol-incr` | `gi`/`zi`/`gzi` family unchanged |
| `0` | `go-leftmost` | *(was unbound)* | — |
| `$` | `go-rightmost` | `type-currency` | `z$` (same char, `z` prefix) |
| `_` | `go-leftmost` | `resize-col-max` | `zw` (z + **W**idth) |
| `^` | `go-leftmost` | `rename-col` | `zN` (z + **N**ame) |

`gh` / `gl` remain bound to go-leftmost/go-rightmost as the non-overloaded canonical fallback. The `z`-prefix slots (`z$`, `zw`, `zN`) were verified empty before binding so we don't clobber any default — and the existing `z_` (resize-col-input), `z^` (rename-col-selected), `g^` (rename-cols-row), `gz_` (resize-cols-input) family is fully intact.

**Trade-off you should know about**: `0` / `_` / `^` all alias to `go-leftmost`. Strict vim differentiates `_` (first non-blank) from `^` (first visible non-blank), but VisiData has no "first non-blank cell" concept so they collapse onto the same column-leftmost semantic.

## Data safety for read-only scenarios — `vd-ro`

New shell alias `vd-ro='visidata --readonly'` in `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh`. VisiData's protection model has three layers worth keeping in mind:

1. **No auto-save, ever.** Edits live in deferred buffers (`Sheet._deferredAdds` / `_deferredMods` / `_deferredDels` per `visidata/modify.py`). Closing with `q` / `Q` / `gq` discards them. You must explicitly press `Ctrl+S` (save-as, new path) or `g Ctrl+S` (save to source) to commit.
2. **`--readonly` blocks the save path.** `vd.optalias('readonly', 'overwrite', 'n')` makes `confirmOverwrite()` fail with `'overwrite disabled'`. In-memory edits stay allowed (so you can still prototype filters / annotations), but the change can't be written back. This is the layer `vd-ro` adds — belt-and-suspenders over the no-auto-save guarantee.
3. **Pair with `vd-arrow` for `.feather`.** `visidata --readonly -f arrow file.feather` gets you both the StringDtype workaround and the save-block. The `dot_visidatarc.tmpl` reroute already makes `-f arrow` redundant for `.feather` on managed hosts, but it's a useful belt for ad-hoc machines or `.arrow` inputs.

Use it like:

```bash
vd-ro data.feather                 # inspect-only
vd-ro -f arrow upstream.feather    # inspect-only + force ArrowSheet
vd-ro logs/server.log              # safe colleague-file inspection
```

## Files touched

- `dot_visidatarc.tmpl` — extended the `{{ if .enableVimMode }}` block with 4 column-nav bindings + 3 relocations; added expository tables and rationale.
- `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` — added `vd-ro` alias with full protection-model explanation in comments.
- `docs/shells/aliases.md` — new `## Data Viewers` section with `vd-arrow` + `vd-ro` rows (fixes a pre-existing gap where `vd-arrow` was never documented); TOC updated.
- `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` — rewrote the VisiData subsection from "single rebind" → multi-part (INSERT mnemonic / Column navigation / Data safety / Why no broader gating / Why `~/.visidatarc`); updated catalog row to reflect the wider scope; updated the `enableVimMode=false` bullet to list every default that stays intact.

- Runtime probe against the rendered rc (loaded the way VisiData itself does in `loadConfigFile`): all 8 bindings resolve correctly via `prettykeys()` normalization (`zN` → `zShift+N` internally, dispatches to `rename-col`).
- With `enableVimMode=false`: `$` → `type-currency`, `_` → `resize-col-max`, `^` → `rename-col`, `i` → `addcol-incr`, `0` unbound, and `z$`/`zw`/`zN` all return `None` — defaults fully preserved, feather override still active.
- `vd.couldOverwrite()` correctly returns `False` after `options.overwrite='n'`, confirming `--readonly` blocks the save path.
